parts.label: a
parts.technique: Simple random sampling using random numbers
parts.reason: S1.1 explicitly covers simple random sampling and use of random number techniques to select a sample.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Stratified sampling
parts.reason: S1.1 explicitly lists stratified sampling as a technique students must be familiar with.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Critique of simple random sampling / identifying under-represented groups
parts.reason: S1.1 covers understanding sampling techniques including critiquing them and reasoning about which groups may be missed; this matches directly.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
parts.reason: No statement mentions Spearman's rank correlation; only PMCC (r) is mentioned in S5.1 and its formula use is excluded. Spearman's rank is a distinct named concept not covered anywhere.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test using Spearman's rank correlation critical value
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec Spearman's rank coefficient from (a); also Spearman's test itself is not a statement (only PMCC correlation testing per S5.1, which excludes formula calculation but the test itself for rho is PMCC-based, not Spearman's).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Correlation does not imply causation
parts.reason: Depends on prior out-of-spec parts (a)/(b); also this is a general comment not tied to any statement about causation vs correlation for regression/Spearman context (S2.2 mentions correlation not causation but this question is about Spearman's rank result specifically).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test
parts.reason: Chi-squared tests are not mentioned in any statement; S5 only covers binomial proportion and Normal mean tests.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Chi-squared test hypotheses for association
parts.reason: Chi-squared test for association is not covered by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Expected frequency calculation for contingency table
parts.reason: This is part of the chi-squared association test method, not covered by any statement.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Degrees of freedom for contingency table with pooling
parts.reason: Part of chi-squared methodology, not in spec.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Chi-squared test conclusion
parts.reason: Part of chi-squared methodology, not in spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Confidence interval for population mean (known variance)
parts.reason: No statement describes construction of confidence intervals; S5.3 covers hypothesis testing for the mean, not confidence intervals, so this named technique is absent.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Two-sample z-test for difference of means (known variances)
parts.reason: S5.3 only describes a one-sample test for the mean of a Normal distribution with known variance; a two-sample test comparing two independent means is not described by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: One-sample z-test structure (known variance) applied separately to each sample to bound mu
parts.reason: This part uses the same one-sample z-statistic (X-μ)/(σ/√n) ~ N(0,1) structure described in S5.3, applied independently to each sample; it does not rely on the out-of-spec two-sample test in (b).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test for Normal distribution
parts.reason: Chi-squared tests are not mentioned in any statement.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Unbiased estimates of mean and variance from summary statistics (Σx, Σx²)
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculating mean and standard deviation (including unbiased S=√(Sxx/(n-1))) from summary statistics; this matches directly.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test (with estimated parameters, reduced df)
parts.reason: Chi-squared testing is not covered by any statement.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation using estimated mean/variance
parts.reason: S4.2 covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution; using the in-spec mean/variance from part (b) to find P(X>7) is a standard Normal probability calculation.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Distribution of the difference of two independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: No statement covers linear combinations (sums/differences) of independent Normal random variables; S4.2 only covers Normal distribution as a single-variable model, not combinations.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Distribution of a linear combination of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: Same as (a): combining independent normal variables (sums, scalar multiples) is not described by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Optimisation of variance for a linear combination aR+bY subject to constraint on mean
parts.reason: Requires the same out-of-spec concept of linear combinations of independent Normal random variables and their variance; not covered by any statement.
